title: build-inspector-probes-report-to-the-watch
intention: Every standing WATCHME probe berthed in cairn/machines/build_inspector reports to harbor_master's watch verb with {ticket, holds, finding} stated against its own ticket's falsifier, and each spec names that receiver.
why: Every standing probe in cairn/machines/build_inspector mails with no verb and nothing uses it (835b5736bf2b D2); a88d6a368cfb built the watch verb that uses a WATCHME finding and 8ecb99998254 built watch_carry. Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: 835b5736bf2b's falsifier (zero probe-bearing standing specs lack a receiver) and Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it; RULE 1 (the build stays inside cairn/machines/build_inspector; base's helper through its public interface, harbor_master through its bus verb)
how: Measured 2026-10-03: 3 tickets at a rest carry a watchme probe under cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/ (18f33ae50f02, 2744aab73ff3, ff2869a09043). Read 2026-10-03: four standing tickets carry a probe under cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes. Three (18f33ae50f02 does_the_derivation_keep_up, 2744aab73ff3 does_the_denied_set_stay_put, ff2869a09043 does_the_address_gate_bite) have fails-shaped triggers (TRUE on the wrong-shape signal, a hole, a denied gain, a gate gone or not biting, or a vacuous reading) and already post to='harbor_master' with no verb, so they gain verb 'watch' and none retargets. The fourth, d48d54dccde6's unattributed_definitional_claims, fires while the claim_provenance sieve is registered and neither ~/.cairn/devices/build_inspector/0/claim_provenance_caught.json nor ..._missed.json exists; the sieve IS registered, and nothing in cairn, skills or bin writes either marker (grep 2026-10-03), so its watch can never conclude and no receiver can use its data — the b0c0c47835c1 precedent under 8ecb99998254 (D7): its ticket goes to FIXME through the watch verb with that finding. No proof imports a build_inspector probe. Each PROBE gets verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry(<its id>, _carry, <its predicate>), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe (declared public). Each ticket's watchme spec gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} through the artifact door. A proof under cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs reads the population from the commons and asserts each probe's verb, to, and live payload invariants.
falsifier: GREEN when every ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme.probe sits under cairn/machines/build_inspector has a probe whose PROBE posts verb 'watch' to 'harbor_master' and whose payload over live data carries ticket == that ticket's id, holds a bool, and a non-empty finding whenever holds is False; and every such spec names receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} with watchme_spec_error naming no receiver fault. RED if any standing build_inspector spec lacks the receiver, or if a converted payload's ticket is a path or another id. WRONG INTENT if a build_inspector probe's data has a reader other than its own ticket's FIXME that only Akien could name.
watchme: none, because what this child's probes say is read by harbor_master's watch verb (a88d6a368cfb, PROVED), and whether they ever fire is 164da559823d's and acb4ecd84364's watch (CairnCommons/tickets/164da559823d-*.json); a probe on probes reporting would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is 3 PROBE declarations and their specs, all inside cairn/machines/build_inspector.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which probes and how: 18f33ae50f02 does_the_derivation_keep_up (fails=_trigger), 2744aab73ff3 does_the_denied_set_stay_put (fails=_trigger), ff2869a09043 does_the_address_gate_bite (fails=_trigger). In each file under cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/: append watch_carry to the existing 'from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...' line; use the probe's id constant (named per probe below, added as `_TICKET_ID = "<id>"` after the import block when absent); in PROBE = Probe(...) replace 'carry=_carry,' with 'verb="watch",' and 'carry=watch_carry(<const>, _carry, <pred>),'. Each holds _OWNING_TICKET as a slug, not the id; that constant stays as it is, and a new _TICKET_ID carries the 12-hex id for watch_carry. The fourth standing probe, unattributed_definitional_claims (d48d54dccde6), is NOT converted: see the unreceivable decision. Nothing else in a probe changes. (2) watch_carry exists in cairn/tools/base/probe.py (8ecb99998254); do not edit it. (3) Specs: each ticket's watchme spec whose probe starts with cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/ gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}, through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write. (4) Proof: cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch.py, PROVES {'817a2890b0de': {'all': 'test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}, modeled on cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py. (5) Every proof that imports a converted probe stays green: run them.

decisions.text: D1: the probes — In each of these files under cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/: does_the_derivation_keep_up.py (18f33ae50f02: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; fails=_trigger), does_the_denied_set_stay_put.py (2744aab73ff3: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; fails=_trigger), does_the_address_gate_bite.py (ff2869a09043: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; fails=_trigger) — append watch_carry to the existing `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line; where the constant is to be added, add `_TICKET_ID = "<its id>"` after the import block; in `PROBE = Probe(...)` replace `carry=_carry,` with `verb="watch",` and `carry=watch_carry(<constant>, _carry, <its predicate>),`. Each holds _OWNING_TICKET as a slug, not the id; that constant stays as it is, and a new _TICKET_ID carries the 12-hex id for watch_carry. The fourth standing probe, unattributed_definitional_claims (d48d54dccde6), is NOT converted: see the unreceivable decision. Nothing else changes; watch_carry is not edited.

D3: the proof — Create cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch.py: a copy of cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py with the docstring naming cairn/machines/build_inspector and ticket 817a2890b0de; PROVES = {'817a2890b0de': {'all': 'test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}; BERTH = 'cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/'; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] (the repo root: the directory holding cairn/); teeth renamed test_every_standing_build_inspector_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_build_inspector_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch. Structure, in full: imports importlib, json, subprocess, sys, Path; _REPO_ROOT on sys.path; parse_workflow from cairn.tools.base.transitions; watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec; _main_tree() = Path(git -C _REPO_ROOT rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).parent falling back to _REPO_ROOT; _tickets() = _main_tree().parent/'CairnCommons'/'tickets'; _standing() = (id, doc, spec) for each ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme spec's probe starts with BERTH, asserting non-empty; the posts tooth imports each probe module and asserts PROBE.verb == 'watch', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', payload({}) carries ticket == the id, holds a bool, non-empty finding when holds is False (invariants only); the receiver tooth asserts spec['receiver'] == {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} and watchme_spec_error(doc) names no receiver fault; a __main__ block runs each, prints PASS/FAIL, exits 1 on any failure. No classes.

D4: the specs' receiver — Ticket files are /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json (glob '<id>-*.json', exactly one). For each of 18f33ae50f02, 2744aab73ff3, ff2869a09043: doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text()); the watchme is a dict or list of dicts; the spec whose 'probe' starts with 'cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/' gets spec['receiver'] = {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; then cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(p, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='<id>: the watchme names its receiver, harbor_master\'s watch verb (817a2890b0de)') — write(path, text, *, verb, why), text the WHOLE modified ticket. Run it as a script file (a shell command naming a record path and writing is refused by the artifact gate).

D5: green, seal, commit — Run cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (exit 0) and the probe-importing proofs (none found by grep); each must be green. Seal with `bin/cairn test --seal --timeout 900 cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_build_inspector_probes_report_to_the_watch.py <the probe-importing proofs>` (it runs each and writes its validation beside it). Commit with message '817a2890b0de: build_inspector probes report to the watch' (the commit runs the reseal ladder, so allow an hour); commit the commons.

D6: the unreceivable probe — d48d54dccde6's probe cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/unattributed_definitional_claims.py is not edited and its spec gets no receiver. Instead, after the three conversions, post one finding to harbor_master's watch verb as a scratch script: from cairn.tools.bus_client import reach; reach('harbor_master').request(sender='cc', to='harbor_master', verb='watch', why='<this ticket id>: no receiver can use this probe', body={'ticket': 'd48d54dccde6', 'holds': False, 'finding': "its probe unattributed_definitional_claims waits for claim_provenance_caught.json or claim_provenance_missed.json under ~/.cairn/devices/build_inspector/0/, and nothing in cairn, skills or bin writes either (grep 2026-10-03), while the claim_provenance sieve is registered — the watch can never conclude and no receiver can use its data (Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: no sensible receiver -> FIXME)"}). The reply must be accepted, and d48d54dccde6's workflow_and_state must then read [FIXME. That takes it out of the proof's standing population (PROVED or WATCHME only), so the proof needs no exclusion.

_standing() ASSERTS the population is non-empty, as in the pattern proof (cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py): after the loop, `assert out, f"no standing ticket names a probe under {BERTH} — the population vanished"`. An empty population is a red, never a silent pass.

The builder never edits d48d54dccde6's workflow_and_state: harbor_master's watch verb, on accepting {holds: False}, moves the ticket's cursor itself (clearance writes it back through the artifact door — the b0c0c47835c1 precedent, 2026-10-03). The builder only READS the file afterwards and checks that the string '[FIXME' appears in workflow_and_state (e.g. '... -> [FIXME:...] -> ...'); the proof's unreceivable tooth asserts the same substring plus a fixme entry with kind 'watchme'. If the reply is not accepted or the substring is absent, that is a red to fix, not to work around.

The watch verb moves the cursor itself (harbor_master device.py _handle_watch calls clearance._send_to_fixme): the builder posts reach("harbor_master").request(sender="cc", to="harbor_master", verb="watch", why=..., body={"ticket": <id>, "holds": False, "finding": <finding>}), reads the reply body (reply.get("body", reply)), requires body["accepted"] is True and body["acted"] == "fixme", then requires the substring "[FIXME" in the ticket file's workflow_and_state. The builder never writes workflow_and_state by hand; the exact rendered syntax is clearance's, and the proof tooth test_the_unreceivable_probes_sent_their_tickets_to_fixme asserts only that substring plus a fixme entry of kind "watchme".

The proof is a byte-for-byte copy (cp) of cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py carrying only the modifications this ticket lists; _standing() ends with `assert out, f"no standing ticket names a probe under {BERTH} — the population vanished"` (an AssertionError, never silent), and _main_tree/_tickets are the concrete code in that template.

The receiver is set by ONE Python script file the builder writes in the session scratchpad and runs: for each ticket id it globs the one ticket file, json-loads it, sets spec["receiver"] on every watchme spec whose probe starts with the berth path, and calls cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", verb="cast", why=...). A shell command naming a record path while writing is refused by the artifact gate, which is why it is a script file.

The proof is created by copying the existing file cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py byte for byte (cp), then making ONLY the modifications this ticket lists (docstring, PROVES, BERTH, _REPO_ROOT depth, the three tooth names, plus any tooth this ticket adds). No generator script exists or is used. The posts tooth obtains each payload as PROBE.payload({}) — Probe.payload runs the carry over that context.

The template cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py exists on disk (sealed green under ticket 8d3c36e1fe59); it has teeth test_every_standing_inference_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_inference_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch, which are copied and renamed as stated.
